data.title: RBI opens special dollar window for three state-run oil marketing companies
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), on October 10, announced a special window to meet the entire daily dollar requirements of three public sector oil marketing companies (OMCs), as the central bank moves to ensure orderly functioning of the foreign exchange market.

The facility will be available to Indian Oil Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Bharat Petroleum Corporation from October 12 and will remain in place until further notice, the RBI said in a press release.

Under the arrangement, the RBI will sell US dollars to the three companies through designated banks. The central bank said the decision was taken after assessing current market conditions.

The announcement comes amid evolving conditions in the foreign exchange market. Separately, the RBI on October 10 tightened rules governing rupee-linked foreign exchange derivatives, including restrictions on rebooking cancelled contracts and a reduction in the threshold for undertaking certain derivative transactions without establishing underlying exposure.

The RBI said the measures were intended to strengthen market discipline and ensure appropriate risk management while maintaining an orderly and transparent foreign exchange market.

data.title: Bitcoin's volatility is falling, but its extreme price swings now outpace 2018
data.description:
Bitcoin has never looked calmer on paper. Its annualized realized volatility has settled into a range of 40% to 47% in 2026, a sharp drop from historical averages above 80%.

The catch is that the calm average hides something stranger underneath. According to CoinDesk, extreme price swings are now happening more often than they did in 2018, one of the most chaotic years in the asset's history.

Realized volatility measures how much an asset's price actually moved over a given period. Bitcoin's version of that figure now sits between 40% and 47% on an annualized basis, compared to earlier market cycles that routinely produced volatility readings above 80%.

Implied volatility has followed the same downward path. That figure comes from options prices and reflects how much movement traders expect going forward. Both the backward-looking and forward-looking gauges have been trending lower heading into 2026.

Then there is the less comfortable statistic. Volatility tied to sudden price jumps has climbed by 71% compared to the first year of spot Bitcoin ETF trading. Those jumps are the tail events, the moves far outside a normal day's range, and they are now landing more frequently than they did in 2018.

Bitcoin hit an all-time high around $126,200 in October 2025. From there, it slid to lows near $58,000 by mid-2026, a drawdown of approximately 53-54%.

Previous cycles saw the asset shed 70-82% after hitting a peak. As of early October 2026, Bitcoin was trading at roughly $85,000, leaving it about 32% below the prior year's peak.

The pattern now emerging has been described as staircase-style price action. Bitcoin climbs gradually, step by step, then drops abruptly when a correction hits.

That shape explains how average volatility and extreme swings can both move in opposite directions at once. Most days are quiet, which drags the average down. The sharp corrections, when they arrive, are concentrated and sudden, which pushes the tail-event count up.

The shift traces back to the post-2024 ETF era. Spot Bitcoin ETFs opened the door for institutional capital to flow into the asset through familiar brokerage accounts. Institutional participation has helped limit cascading liquidations, where leveraged positions get forcibly closed, triggering more selling and further forced closures. Fewer of those dominoes means shorter corrections and shallower overall drawdowns.

For long-term investors, shallower drawdowns of around 53% compared to historical drops of 70-82% make Bitcoin easier to size into a diversified portfolio without one bad year sinking the whole strategy.

For active traders, low average volatility can encourage taking on more leverage, since daily swings feel manageable. When a tail event arrives, those positions are exactly the ones that get wiped out. The 71% rise in jump volatility since the first ETF year suggests that risk has grown, not shrunk.

If implied volatility keeps falling while sudden jumps keep rising, it could mean the market is underpricing the chance of a sharp move. Traders who sell options to collect premium in quiet conditions would be most exposed to that gap.

Buyers waiting for a classic 80% crash to load up may find this cycle does not deliver one. The drop from roughly $126,200 to near $58,000 shows the asset can still cut its value in half within months, but Bitcoin is spending more time behaving like a mature macro asset while its sharpest moments are arriving more often than in 2018.

data.title: TCS Earnings Spark IT Rally As Investors Eye Demand Recovery
data.description:
Nifty IT rises 3.02 per cent after TCS beats quarterly earnings estimates, while AI disruption and US labour curbs remain sector concerns

Indian IT stocks rallied on Friday, 9 October, after Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reported better-than-expected second-quarter results, lifting hopes of a recovery in technology demand. The Nifty IT index rose 3.02 per cent, while TCS shares advanced 3.85 per cent to close at Rs 2,156 on the NSE.

The gains followed a prolonged correction in technology stocks, with concerns over client spending, artificial intelligence (AI) disruption and US labour restrictions weighing on sentiment. TCS’s results provided a fresh catalyst for buying, although a single session’s gains do not establish a sustained recovery across the sector.

TCS Results Lift IT Stocks

TCS shares rose as much as 6 per cent during Friday’s session before closing at Rs 2,156. The stock had declined about 30 per cent over the preceding year, the steepest fall among Nifty 50 constituents, according to media reports. The Nifty 50 gained 1.3 per cent on Friday. The company reported consolidated net profit of Rs 13,884 crore for the July-September quarter of FY27, up 14.9 per cent from Rs 12,075 crore a year earlier. Revenue from operations increased 11.2 per cent to Rs 73,188 crore, compared with Rs 65,799 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26.

Valuations And Demand Remain In Focus

The rally also came after a difficult period for IT stocks. Attractive valuations helped support sentiment, while investors assessed whether the latest results signalled an improvement in technology spending. However, TCS’s quarterly performance alone does not establish that demand has recovered across the industry. Results and management commentary from other IT services companies will provide further indications of the strength and breadth of any improvement.

AI remains both an opportunity and a challenge for technology services providers. The sector faces questions about how AI-led automation could affect traditional services, even as companies pursue opportunities related to AI adoption. The implications for revenue and profitability will depend on how demand, pricing and delivery models evolve.

US Labour Restrictions Remain A Concern

The rally came amid scrutiny of US employment-based immigration processes, including the reported suspension of the PERM labour-certification process involving several technology companies. PERM is associated with certain employment-based green-card applications and should not be confused with a blanket suspension of all US work visas.

The policy developments remain a consideration for Indian IT companies with US operations. Their exposure will vary according to hiring practices, workforce requirements and the extent to which they rely on employment-based permanent residency applications. Friday’s market gains indicate an improvement in investor sentiment following TCS’s results, but do not establish that concerns over immigration policy or AI disruption have been resolved.

Broader Recovery Awaits Confirmation

TCS’s earnings provided a near-term boost to IT stocks after a steep correction. The Nifty IT index rose 3.02 per cent on Friday, while the benchmark Nifty 50 gained 1.3 per cent. Whether the rally develops into a sustained sector recovery will depend on subsequent earnings, management commentary and evidence of improving demand across the industry.

data.title: Musk Takes Dig At Ambani Over Starlink’s India Entry, Alleges Monopoly
data.description:
Elon Musk’s ‘Prime Minister Ambani’ jibe intensifies the dispute over Starlink’s entry into India, bringing competition and regulatory approvals in the satellite internet market into focus

Elon Musk has taken a fresh swipe at Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani over Starlink’s proposed entry into India, sarcastically addressing the billionaire as “Prime Minister Ambani” amid allegations that established business interests are restricting competition in the satellite internet market.

In a post on social media platform X, the SpaceX chief wrote: “Dear Prime Minister Ambani, please accept my humble apologies for not realising that you are the real boss of India.”

The remark escalates the public dispute surrounding Starlink’s commercial launch in India, where Reliance Jio and Bharti Airtel are also seeking opportunities in the satellite communications market.

Musk has argued that Starlink could expand internet access in underserved regions, connect remote communities and create new opportunities for education and small businesses. However, the company’s commercial operations in India remain subject to regulatory approvals and compliance requirements.

Musk Questions Delays In Starlink’s India Launch

Musk’s latest remarks follow his criticism of the time taken to secure approval for Starlink’s India operations.

The entrepreneur has said the company has spent years complying with Indian government requirements and questioned why it has yet to commence commercial services in the country.

He has also alleged that powerful business interests are seeking to protect existing market positions by restricting Starlink’s entry. Musk’s comments have particularly drawn attention to the competitive dynamics involving India’s established telecommunications operators.

However, his allegations against Ambani have not been independently substantiated.

Starlink, operated by Musk’s SpaceX, uses a network of low-Earth-orbit satellites to deliver broadband connectivity. The technology can provide internet access in areas where conventional mobile networks and fibre-optic infrastructure are difficult or expensive to deploy.

Government Defends Satellite Internet Approval Process

The dispute has brought renewed attention to India’s regulatory framework for satellite communications.

The government has maintained that satellite internet providers must meet the applicable licensing, security and other regulatory requirements before commencing commercial operations. It has rejected allegations that the approval process is designed to favour established telecom operators.

Security clearances and compliance requirements remain important considerations for companies seeking to offer satellite-based communication services in India.

The central issue is whether Starlink can complete the necessary approvals and enter the market on terms that allow it to compete with existing and prospective service providers.

Reliance Jio And Airtel Eye Satellite Connectivity

India is an important potential market for satellite broadband, given its large population and the continuing need to improve connectivity in remote and underserved areas.

Reliance Jio, part of Ambani-led Reliance Industries, and Bharti Airtel, led by Sunil Bharti Mittal, are also pursuing opportunities in satellite communications.

Starlink’s entry could increase competition and expand the range of connectivity options available to consumers, businesses and institutions, particularly in locations with limited terrestrial broadband infrastructure.

The prospect of additional competition has also intensified debate over spectrum allocation, licensing conditions and the regulatory treatment of satellite internet providers.

Starlink’s India Entry Remains In Focus

Starlink has been pursuing access to the Indian market for several years, positioning its satellite network as an alternative for customers who lack reliable conventional broadband connectivity.

A commercial launch could open up opportunities across remote households, businesses, educational institutions and other users requiring dependable internet access.

However, the timing of the launch will depend on the company meeting the necessary regulatory requirements.

Musk’s latest comments have sharpened the public debate over competition and market access in India’s telecommunications sector. The outcome of Starlink’s regulatory process could have wider implications for the development of satellite broadband services and the competitive landscape of the country’s internet market.

data.title: Public Sector Banks Raise Repo-Linked Lending Rates By 25 Bps After RBI Hike
data.description:
The move will increase borrowing costs for existing and new external benchmark-linked loans as banks reprice lending rates

Several domestic banks have raised their repo-linked lending rates by 25 basis points (bps) after the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) increased the policy repo rate to 5.5 per cent. The move is set to increase borrowing costs for customers with loans linked to external benchmarks.

Bank of Baroda (BoB), Punjab National Bank (PNB), Indian Bank, Indian Overseas Bank (IOB), Bank of India (BoI) and RBL Bank have revised their benchmark-linked lending rates following the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) decision. The revisions will affect both new borrowers and existing customers whose loans are linked to external benchmarks.

BoB has raised its Baroda Repo Based Lending Rate by 25 bps to 8.15 per cent from 7.90 per cent. With the repo rate now at 5.5 per cent, the revised rate represents a spread of 2.65 percentage points over the RBI’s policy rate.

PNB has increased its repo-linked lending rate to 8.35 per cent from 8.10 per cent. Indian Bank has raised its Repo-Linked Benchmark Lending Rate to 8.20 per cent from 7.95 per cent, with the revised rate effective October 8.

IOB has also increased its repo-linked lending rate by 25 bps to 8.35 per cent from 8.10 per cent. BoI has raised its Repo-Based Lending Rate to 8.35 per cent from 8.10 per cent, while RBL Bank’s repo-linked lending rate stood at 8.50 per cent as of October 7.

UCO Bank has revised several benchmark-linked rates with effect from October 8. Its three-month Benchmark Lending Rate (BLR) has increased to 5.30 per cent from 5.25 per cent, while the six-month Treasury Bill Linked Rate (TBLR) has risen to 5.70 per cent from 5.55 per cent.

The bank has raised its 12-month TBLR to 5.95 per cent from 5.70 per cent. Its one-year government securities-linked rate has increased to 6.26 per cent from 5.88 per cent, while the 10-year Gsec-linked rate has moved up to 7.32 per cent from 7.09 per cent.

UCO Bank has also raised the repo-linked rate for UCO Float to 8.30 per cent from 8.05 per cent. The repo-linked rate for UCO Prime has been increased to 5.50 per cent from 5.25 per cent.

Borrowers Face Higher Costs

For new loans linked to external benchmarks such as the repo rate, the 25-bps increase will be transmitted immediately through the applicable lending rate. Existing external benchmark-linked loans will also be repriced upwards by a similar amount, typically within 90 days.

The impact on deposit rates is expected to emerge more gradually. Banks currently have additional liquidity from foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR(B)) deposits, which could reduce the immediate pressure to increase rates across their existing deposit base.

However, banks may offer higher rates on fresh deposits if short-term money market rates remain elevated. This could gradually increase funding costs as banks seek to attract new deposits.

RBI Takes Hawkish Stance

The lending rate revisions follow Wednesday’s MPC decision to raise the policy repo rate by 25 bps to 5.5 per cent. The six-member panel unanimously supported the rate increase, which was broadly in line with market expectations.

The bigger policy shift came through the change in stance from “neutral” to “calibrated tightening”. Four MPC members supported the change, while external members Ram Singh and Nagesh Kumar favoured retaining the neutral stance.

RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra indicated a hawkish outlook, stating that rate cuts were off the table in the near term. He said future policy action could involve either a rate hike or a pause, depending on evolving economic conditions and the outlook.

data.title: Fuel Cost Pressures Trigger Fresh Surcharge Hikes Across Airlines
data.description:
Higher aviation turbine fuel costs prompt airlines to revise surcharges, increasing travel expenses for passengers

Air India, Air India Express and Akasa Air have raised fuel surcharges as rising aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices increase airline operating costs. The revisions come amid volatility in global energy markets and add to the cost of air travel for passengers.

Air India’s revised domestic surcharge ranges from Rs 400 for flights covering up to 500 km to Rs 1,200 for journeys exceeding 2,000 km. On international routes, the surcharge ranges from USD 55 for West Asia to USD 215 for North America.

“ATF prices have witnessed significant volatility in recent months, driven largely by geopolitical developments and sustained pressure on global energy markets. The latest increase in fuel prices has further elevated operating costs for airlines, with fuel continuing to account for a substantial proportion of overall airline expenditure,” Air India said in a statement.

Akasa Revises Fuel Charges

Akasa Air has increased its domestic fuel surcharge, with the minimum charge rising from Rs 199 to Rs 375 and the maximum charge increasing from Rs 1,300 to Rs 2,500, according to a media report. The revised charges add to the cost of air travel for passengers booking tickets under the new rates. The changes follow a similar move by IndiGo, which had earlier raised its fuel surcharge. The revisions across airlines come as higher ATF prices add to operating expenses.

Higher Costs Push Up Fares

Fuel accounts for a substantial share of airline operating expenditure, making carriers vulnerable to fluctuations in ATF prices. Geopolitical developments and volatility in global energy markets have added to cost pressures, prompting airlines to revise their surcharges. The higher charges increase the amount passengers pay for new bookings, with the additional cost varying by airline, route, and distance.

data.title: Indian Retail Braced For Subdued Q2 As Festive Shift Hits Apparel
data.description:
Value retail and premium footwear offset delayed festive demand and input cost headwinds, reports Elara Capital

Indian consumer discretionary retail companies are projected to deliver an aggregate revenue growth of 11.8 per cent year-on-year in the second quarter of FY27, even as an unfavourable calendar shift and lingering raw material inflation weigh on the apparel segment. Operating profit (Ebitda) across the sector is forecast to expand by 12.7 per cent, underpinned by strong performances in value retail, footwear, and innerwear.

According to a quarterly preview report by Mumbai-based brokerage Elara Securities, the shift of the festive season into the third quarter has sharply curtailed demand for traditional and mid-market apparel.

Navratri, which commenced on 22 September in 2025, moves entirely into the October quarter this fiscal year, compounded by the pre-festive Shraddh period that delayed consumer purchases late into September.

Festive Distortion Weighs on Apparel

The resulting calendar distortion has left the broader apparel category facing an estimated 3.8 per cent contraction in revenue and a 5.0 per cent drop in Ebitda, dragged down by operating deleverage and higher input prices.

Ethnic and specialised retailers are bearing the brunt: bridal and celebration wear specialist Vedant Fashions is expected to report a 5.6 per cent drop in revenue to Rs  2,483 million alongside an 8.0 per cent fall in adjusted profit after tax (PAT), while Go Fashion is projected to post a 1.6 per cent revenue drop and a 26.9 per cent decline in adjusted earnings. Same-store sales growth (SSSG) for both firms remains anaemic at 1.0 per cent and -0.6 per cent respectively.

Value Formats Defy Broader Slump

In contrast, value and mass-market formats continue to display robust momentum. Budget department chain Vishal Mega Mart is forecast to post a 17.5 per cent year-on-year rise in revenue to Rs  35,032 million, propelled by 6.0 per cent SSSG and an aggressive rollout of 25 new stores during the quarter. Adjusted PAT for the retailer is slated to increase by 17.7 per cent to Rs  1,793 million.

Footwear Gains on Premiumisation

The footwear sector is likewise maintaining resilient expansion, supported by brand premiumisation and disciplined price increases. Aggregate footwear coverage is tracking an 8.8 per cent top-line increase and 10.0 per cent Ebitda growth.

Metro Brands leads the cohort with an estimated 13.2 per cent revenue increase and a 21.9 per cent rise in adjusted profit, while Campus Activewear is pencilled in for a 30.7 per cent surge in adjusted profit. Bata India is seen delivering modest revenue growth of 3.5 per cent, though lower discounting and strict cost controls are expected to drive a 37.5 per cent rebound in adjusted net earnings.

Margin Squeeze in Innerwear and Luggage

Elsewhere, innerwear brands are riding volume recoveries despite margin squeezes caused by the consumption of high-cost cotton inventory. Market leader Page Industries is projected to deliver an 11.8 per cent top-line improvement, aided by product introductions and price hikes flowing through the supply chain.

In luggage, Safari Industries and turnaround candidate VIP Industries are expanding sales by 11.0 per cent and 10.8 per cent respectively, though elevated promotions, advertising outlays, and crude-linked polymer resin costs continue to compress operating margins.

Overall sector Ebitda margins are forecast to tick up by 13 basis points to 15.5 per cent, as gains from operating leverage across scaled players compensate for cotton and petrochemical inflation. Elara Capital identified Metro Brands, Campus Activewear, and Vishal Mega Mart as its top picks across the coverage universe.

data.title: How can lift irrigation projects help India take water to more farms?
data.description:
India’s irrigation challenge is increasingly becoming a question of water distribution and accessibility, rather than only water availability. More than 80 per cent of India’s available water resources are used for agriculture, yet only around half of the country’s net sown area has access to irrigation.

This is where lift irrigation can play an important role. Conventional canal systems work most effectively where terrain allows water to move by gravity. However, India’s agricultural landscape includes many regions located at higher elevations or across difficult terrain. Lift irrigation enables water to move beyond the natural reach of gravity through pumping systems, rising mains, pipelines and distribution networks.

Taking water beyond the reach of gravity

The objective of lift irrigation is not simply to pump water, but to create a reliable, engineered system that takes water from the source to the command area while managing energy consumption, hydraulic losses and long-term operating requirements.

Pumping stations, rising mains, pressure management, delivery systems and distribution networks must work together, with design considerations including terrain, distance, elevation difference, water requirements and the nature of the command area.

Our experience across irrigation and water-resource projects has reinforced the importance of viewing lift irrigation as part of an integrated water-delivery system rather than as an isolated pumping solution.

From irrigation potential to water delivery

The real impact of large irrigation infrastructure is determined by how efficiently water reaches the field. Pressurised pipeline distribution and micro-irrigation systems such as drip and sprinklers can improve water-use efficiency by reducing conveyance losses, evaporation and runoff. Government programmes such as the Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana’s ‘Per Drop More Crop’ initiative have also encouraged wider adoption of micro-irrigation. As of July 2026, more than 115 lakh hectares have been covered under micro-irrigation.

Lift and gravity systems can complement each other

India will need both lift and gravity-based systems depending on geography and project requirements. Where terrain prevents natural flow, lift irrigation becomes indispensable. The Jigaon Lift Irrigation Project in Maharashtra, for instance, is designed to bring water from the Purna River to dry, upland regions of Buldhana and Akola districts. By mechanically lifting water to higher elevations, the project is expected to provide irrigation across 84,240 hectares of agricultural land while also supplying drinking water.

Where topography permits, gravity-based conveyance can provide an energy-efficient alternative. The Sleemanabad Carrier Canal Project in Madhya Pradesh includes an approximately 12-km-long, 10-m-diameter underground irrigation tunnel that carries water across challenging terrain through gravity. The project is expected to support irrigation across approximately 2.45 lakh hectares.

Energy efficiency will be critical

Energy is a key consideration in lift irrigation. Pumping water over large distances and elevations can involve significant power consumption, making pumping efficiency critical over the project’s life. Efficient pumps, appropriate hydraulic design, automation, monitoring and regular maintenance are therefore essential.

Technology can further improve performance. Automated controls, remote monitoring and data-based operating systems can optimise pumping, identify inefficiencies and help ensure that water is delivered according to actual demand.

Building an Integrated Water Network

The future of irrigation infrastructure lies in viewing the entire water cycle rather than individual assets. Storage, dams, tunnels, lift irrigation, pipelines and micro-irrigation are interconnected components whose ultimate purpose is to deliver water reliably to agricultural land.

Ultimately, India needs to move from creating irrigation potential to reliably delivering water to the farm gate. The goal is simple: deliver the right quantity of water to the right place, with minimum losses and maximum reliability.

The author is Managing Director, Patel Engineering Ltd.

data.title: Personal loan rates October 2026: Check EMI and processing fees across 22 lenders
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Are you looking for a personal loan? Have you devised a plan to repay the borrowed funds? This is important because borrowing funds is just the first step in the process. Further, personal loan interest rates can vary widely across lenders, affecting both the monthly EMI and the overall cost of borrowing.

As of today, the rates listed by 22 prominent lending institutions range from 8.90% to 30.50%, depending primarily on the lending institution, the borrower's profile, the loan tenure, and a host of other factors.

For example, for a Rs.5 lakh personal loan with a 5-year tenure, the EMI starts at Rs.10,355 at Axis Bank and Union Bank of India, as per data compiled by Paisabazaar. Bajaj Finserv, on the other hand, has the widest stated interest rate range, from 10% to 30.50%.

For example, Tata Capital lists a flat Rs.49 processing fee, and Kotak Mahindra Bank charges up to 5% of the loan amount. With these aspects in mind, let us look at personal loan rates and applicable EMIs for October 2026.

It is vital for aspiring borrowers to carefully calculate the total cost of borrowing. This is because a lower advertised rate does not necessarily mean a cheaper personal loan. Factors such as the applicable interest rate, EMI, processing fee and other charges must be considered before making a personal loan decision.

Furthermore, the final rate offered may also depend on factors such as credit score, current income, overall debt levels, employment profile and loan amount.

Hence, before proceeding with the submission of their personal loan application, borrowers should look beyond the headline rate, analyse their repayment potential and assess the overall cost of borrowing. Carefully comparing multiple lending institutions can help identify a loan that better suits their long-term economic needs.

Still, in case of doubts it is wise to consult a financial advisor before availing a loan in order to ensure that the best possible borrowing decision is made as per an individuals current financial requirements.

data.title: RBI tightens forex derivative rules, cuts exposure threshold to $5 million from $100 million
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on October 10 tightened rules governing the foreign exchange market, restricting the rebooking of cancelled rupee-linked derivative contracts and sharply reducing the threshold for undertaking certain forex derivative transactions without establishing underlying exposure.

The measures come amid evolving conditions in the foreign exchange market and are aimed at ensuring its orderly functioning, the central bank said in a press release.

Under the revised norms, authorised dealers will not be permitted to allow users to rebook any foreign exchange derivative contract involving the rupee, whether deliverable or non-deliverable, if it was cancelled with an authorised dealer after the issuance of the directions. Rollover of contracts on maturity will continue to be permitted, subject to existing regulatory requirements.

The RBI has also reduced the threshold for undertaking foreign exchange derivative transactions to hedge contracted exposures without establishing the existence of the underlying exposure to $5 million from $100 million. The revised threshold applies across all authorised dealers.

The corresponding limit for taking positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee without establishing underlying exposure has also been lowered to $5 million from $100 million, across all recognised stock exchanges taken together.

Additional checks on exposures

The central bank has tightened documentation requirements to prevent the same underlying exposure from being hedged through multiple authorised dealers.

Authorised dealers will now have to obtain and retain an undertaking from users entering into rupee-linked foreign exchange derivative contracts to hedge contracted exposures, confirming that the same underlying exposure has not been hedged with another authorised dealer.

The RBI has also introduced a Foreign Exchange Risk Reserve (FERR) requirement for certain rupee-linked derivative transactions.

Under the new framework, authorised dealers will be required to maintain a cash reserve with the RBI equivalent to 20 percent of the rupee value of the notional amount of each transaction exceeding $2 million. The requirement applies to rupee-linked foreign exchange derivative contracts undertaken to hedge current account exposures where the user purchases foreign currency against the rupee.

Liquidity management

The RBI is also tightening liquidity conditions through changes to daily cash reserve ratio (CRR) maintenance norms. From the fortnight beginning October 16, banks will have to maintain at least 99 percent of their prescribed CRR on a daily basis, up from 90 percent earlier, although the overall CRR ratio remains unchanged.

The change comes alongside the RBI’s announcement on October 9 of an open market operation (OMO) sale of government securities worth Rs 25,000 crore, scheduled for October 13, to absorb surplus liquidity. Market participants said the higher daily CRR maintenance requirement would reduce banks’ flexibility in managing day-to-day liquidity, alongside the central bank’s OMO sales.

The forex measures are intended to strengthen market discipline and ensure appropriate risk management in the foreign exchange market, while maintaining an orderly and transparent market environment, the RBI said.

data.title: Robinhood Chain transactions fall more than 40% as memecoin trading cools
data.description:
Robinhood Chain's memecoin party is winding down. According to CoinDesk, the network's slowdown has moved beyond fees and into trading activity, with transactions falling more than 40%.

That's a sharp reversal for a chain that only went live on July 1, 2026.

Start with fees, where the drop was most dramatic. Daily fees on Robinhood Chain peaked at approximately $8 million in early September.

By September 16, they had collapsed 97% to about $230,000.

Transactions followed fees lower. Daily transaction counts slid from 13.1 million to 8.9 million by mid-September, a day-over-day decline of roughly 32% on that measure.

The smoothed view is gentler. The seven-day average for transactions dipped only about 6% over the same stretch.

The engine behind both the boom and the bust was memecoin trading. Launches on platforms such as Pons generated heavy gas spending in August and early September, which is what pushed fees so high. Weekly memecoin volume on Pons fell 37% as appetite for high-gas activity cooled.

Decentralized exchange (DEX) volume on the chain held at or above $1 billion daily during mid-September, even as fees cratered.

Daily DEX volume did come down from its peak of around $1.88 billion in mid-September, roughly halving from that high.

Total value locked (TVL) stayed steady at approximately $1 billion through the turbulence. That figure remained resilient into late September and October, even as DEX volume eased.

There was also no visible mass migration to rival networks such as Solana, with user retention appearing stable.

Robinhood Chain is an Ethereum layer-2 network built using Arbitrum Orbit technology. The network carries the weight of its parent company, Robinhood (HOOD).

Activity has also started to diversify beyond memecoins, with new token pools continuing to appear into early October.

The chain also added support for NEAR Intents, which enables cross-chain swaps across more than 180 assets on more than 30 blockchains.

data.title: RBI takes steps to support rupee, opens dollar window for oil companies
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced more measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the currency fell to within striking distance of its record low.

The central bank will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three government oil-marketing companies to ease the pressure on the spot market.

Under such an arrangement, used in times of strain on the currency, the RBI provides oil companies dollars directly from its foreign exchange reserves.

Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum will be allowed to access to access dollars under the facility from Monday, the RBI said.

Forex dealers will not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives, the bank said.

The RBI slashed the limit for positions in exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee to $5 million from $100 million.

The central bank asked forex dealers to maintain a "foreign exchange risk reserve" for all derivative contracts involving the rupee equal to 20% of the notional amount of each transaction.

The RBI has raised dollars and hiked its policy rate, but pressure on the currency has persisted. On Friday, the rupee closed at 96.73 per dollar, barely changed from its previous close, and near its all-time weakest level of 96.96, hit in May.

The rupee rallied in the non-deliverable forward market on Saturday, with the one-month dollar/rupee contract falling about 40 paise in very thin trading, one trader said.

Addressing oil companies' dollar requirements removes one of the largest sources of demand from the FX market, which should help reduce volatility but it will show up in a depletion of reserves, said Dhiraj Nim, FX strategist at ANZ Bank in Mumbai.

data.title: From ‘no’ to the Yellow Revolution
data.description:
A five-year-old boy was selling packets outside a Costco store in Seattle for a Scouts charity fundraiser. Many people said, “No, thank you.” Asked how long he would continue, he replied: “Till 100 people say no to me.” His teacher explained: accept rejection and still approach the next person.

When farmers said: “Let us think about it”

In the early 1990s, oil palm was unfamiliar to Indian farmers. Extension team members of processors travelled village to village, meeting farmers, along with scientists, government officials, financial institution’s representative. They explained the crop, economics, agronomy and support available, distributed literature and followed up.

The common response was: “Let us think about it. We will come back to you.” Often, that meant “no”.

The hesitation was understandable. Oil palm was a perennial crop with unfamiliar requirements and questions around water, productivity, markets and returns. Demonstration plots therefore became critical: Seeing is believing.

If 100 farmers said “no”, the extension team had to approach the 101st. Every rejection demanded better explanation, demonstration and understanding of farmers’ concerns.

From 8,585 hectares to 6.43 lakh hectares

India had only about 8,585 hectares under oil palm in 1991–92. By 2021–22, the area had reached about 3.70 lakh hectares, with annual CPO production around 3.61 lakh tonnes.

The National Mission on Edible Oils–Oil Palm (NMEO-OP), launched in 2021, marked a new phase. Between 2021–22 and 2025–26, another 2.73 lakh hectares were brought under oil palm, taking cumulative coverage to about 6.43 lakh hectares by 31 March 2026.

First came skill

The early years were a period of learning—nursery management, planting material, agronomy, irrigation, harvesting, processing and farmer engagement. India learned to grow oil palm under diverse agro-climatic conditions and within a smallholder system. Successful plantations created confidence.

Skill created scale

Once farmers saw successful plantations and viable returns, confidence spread from farmer to farmer and village to village. Clusters expanded and processing infrastructure became more viable.

Scale was not created by targets alone. It was created by confidence earned in the field.

Scale is now creating speed

The post-2021 period brought acceleration through NMEO-OP, supporting planting material, irrigation, nurseries, maintenance and processing infrastructure.

But the numbers provide an important lesson. Between 2021–22 and 2024–25, oil-palm area increased from about 3.70 to 5.56 lakh hectares—nearly 50%—while annual CPO production increased from about 3.61 to 3.80 lakh tonnes, around 5%.

This should not automatically be interpreted as failure. Much of the newly planted area is still juvenile; oil palm takes several years to reach meaningful production and higher productivity.

The message is clear: Area expansion is not the same as productive expansion. The real measure must be effective areas —land that is suitable, properly planted, adequately irrigated, maintained, supported by competent extension and capable of producing viable yields.

Why oil palm can power India’s Yellow Revolution

Oil palm has the highest vegetable-oil-yielding capability per hectare among major oil crops. Under good management and maturity, around 4 tonnes of CPO per hectare is a realistic benchmark for well-performing plantations.

This gives oil palm an important role in India’s edible-oil strategy and reducing import dependence. But the Yellow Revolution cannot be achieved simply by planting more hectares. Research must focus on farmer and processor needs—water-stress-suited planting material, higher FFB productivity, higher oil content and resource-use efficiency. In newer geographies, particularly the North-East, speed must be calibrated so that land suitability, water, farmer skill, extension and processing develop together.

The greater challenge

India’s greater challenge is not merely to create the largest possible oil-palm area on paper. It is to ensure that effective area across suitable regions becomes a genuine opportunity for the Yellow Revolution.

A plantation merely planted is an area statistic. A plantation that survives, is maintained, bears consistently and produces economically viable FFB is an asset.

The journey ahead should therefore be: SKILL → SCALE → SPEED → EFFECTIVE AREA → PRODUCTIVITY.

The little boy’s lesson applies equally to this industry: rejection is not necessarily the end; it can be the beginning of learning. Farmers who initially said “no” were teachers. Their doubts forced better explanations, hesitation encouraged demonstration and rejection pushed the industry to improve.

India has moved a long way—from 8,585 hectares to 6.43 lakh hectares. The next step is not simply to move faster. It is to move intelligently.

The ultimate measure will not be hectares planted, but productive oil delivered. That is how oil palm can become a powerful pillar of India’s Yellow Revolution.

The author is former CEO-Oil Palm Plantation, Godrej Agrovet Ltd. and Consultant-Palm Oil Production & Plantation Development, Kolkata, West Bengal. Views are personal.

data.title: Mrityunjay Athreya: the unfashionable management guru who shuns jargon for purpose
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- In 1967, when Mrityunjay Athreya returned to India from Harvard Business School, where he had just completed his doctorate in business administration, India's corporate environment was inward-looking and constrained by strict government controls.

The 26-year-old Athreya's return to his homeland, shunning the many lucrative options available to him in the US, came partly from a love for his country but also because he had figured that Indian companies needed strategic thinking and access to management ideas that were transforming the best companies across the world.

Born in 1941 in Tirunelveli, Tamil Nadu, into a large Tamil Brahmin family, his early education was at a Tamil-medium school before the family moved to Chennai, where he went on to study statistics at Loyola College and then won a gold medal on the way to qualifying as a cost accountant. The choice of subjects was driven by the demands of supplementing the family income, and it worked: he immediately got a job with the British engineering company Guest Keen Williams in Calcutta as a cost accountant.

Ambitious and self-confident, Athreya soon applied to American universities for an MBA programme, though his application went with a twist: Athreya argued that, given his degree and professional qualifications, he should get direct admission to a PhD programme. Stanford Graduate School of Business was among those that agreed, and that's where he proceeded as a Hoover Fellow. A year later, he transferred to Harvard as a Ford Fellow.

On completion, influenced by his childhood hero Subhas Chandra Bose, he chose to come back home, recognising the need and the opportunity to transform Indian companies stuck in a strategy rut. To start with, he joined the Indian Institute of Management in Calcutta as an assistant professor, teaching strategic planning and behavioural sciences. Alongside, he also started consulting and was part of a committee in 1971 set up by the government to restructure the floundering Indian Airlines. After six years of teaching and consulting, he went on a three-year sabbatical to teach at the London Business School.

On his return, he set himself up as an independent adviser to companies, associations, governments and NGOs. It was a good time to become a management consultant in India. The likes of McKinsey, BCG, Arthur D. Little and Monitor had little interest in the country.

Starting off with an assignment for Bharat Heavy Electric Ltd, then part of a set of emerging public sector companies, he went on to advise Indian Oil Corporation, NTPC and ONGC, as well as private firms such as Mahindra & Mahindra and Bharat Forge.

It would take another decade for global consulting majors to make their way into the country, and even then they came in with Western models and ideas. By then, Athreya had tested and deployed his own thinking, which stressed that management was more about people, purpose, values and getting everyone to function as a cohesive team.

In the 1990s, amidst the exhilaration of liberalization that brought a rash of multinational consulting firms along with fashionable management jargon, Athreya sounded almost old-school. Yet, when it came to restructuring India's moribund telecom services infrastructure, the government turned to him.

The Athreya Committee's recommendations, including breaking up the monolithic Department of Telecom, opening up some sections of the network to the private sector and the creation of an independent regulator for the sector, laid the foundations for a telecom revolution, perhaps the most successful government-led intervention in the country.

Typical of the man, he again changed track around 2007, increasingly devoting much of his time to the non-profit sector since he believed that civil society was a crucial leg of the trimurti comprising the government and business that was needed to solve the problems of India.

He was also spending more time with Sampradaan, the platform for charitable initiatives by high net worth individuals set up in 1996. Since then, his work has been more about incorporating Indian philosophical ideas like dharma, the Gita and Vedanta into management.

No longer satisfied with offering corporate advice, Athreya, now 85, likes to talk and deal with issues like lessons for Indian industry from China, governance, social enterprises, technology, inequality and climate change.

It is significant that even as many of the management fads of the 1990s and early 2000s have been debunked or heavily caveated, Athreya's more down-to-earth thinking and wisdom has stood the test of time.

data.title: The week in charts: rate hikes, SIP flows, Airtel's tariffs
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- From the Reserve Bank of India raising its key interest rate for the first time since February 2023 to record SIP inflows despite a shaky stock market, a temporary easing in the standoff over flight operations between Mumbai's two airports and airlines, Bharti Airtel raising postpaid tariffs, and India's 85-medal haul at the Asian Games-here is the week's news in numbers.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) raised its key interest rate by 25 basis points, taking the repo rate to 5.5% from 5.25% earlier. This was the first hike by the central bank since February 2023. The RBI also adopted a hawkish stance, signalling that more rate increases could follow as it seeks to contain inflation risks.

The move comes as several major central banks have also turned more cautious on inflation, with higher energy prices and global trade uncertainty adding to price pressures. The rate increase is expected to raise borrowing costs for consumers, including for auto and housing loans, and weigh on credit growth. Economists expect further tightening in India: Yes Bank sees hikes of 1 percentage point in this cycle, while HDFC Bank expects increases of up to 0.75 percentage point.

Monthly inflows into mutual funds through systematic investment plans (SIPs) rose to an all-time high of Rs.32,297 crore in August, showing continued appetite among retail investors despite a shaky stock market. SIPs are periodic investment commitments by retail investors, typically monthly, and tend to be sticky in nature.

However, the record inflows came alongside a sharp rise in the number of SIPs being discontinued or reaching the end of their tenure. Data from industry grouping Amfi showed that 5.38 million SIPs were either discontinued or reached the end of their tenure in August-the most since January 2026. On a relative scale, the ratio of SIPs stopped to SIPs started was around 81% in August, suggesting that more investors were keen to enter the market than those who sought to exit.

The central government has asked Adani Airport Holdings to put on hold its plan to shift a portion of international flights from Mumbai airport to Navi Mumbai airport, temporarily easing a standoff with airlines. Adani operates both airports serving the Mumbai region. The Navi Mumbai airport began commercial operations in December 2025, after which Adani lined up the renovation of Terminal 1 at Mumbai airport.

As part of the plan, it asked airlines to shift one-third of their international flights from Mumbai's Terminal 2 to Navi Mumbai. Airlines, however, said they were not consulted on the proposed move. The Navi Mumbai airport recorded 3,047 aircraft movements in August, compared with 26,017 at Mumbai airport, and has seen aircraft movements decline over the past three months.

26%: The projected year-on-year increase in market borrowings by Indian states in the October-December quarter, to Rs.3.6 trillion, according to Icra.

Rs.28,000: The average price per sq ft of DLF's first senior-living project, The Aureva in Gurugram. All 172 apartments, with a total value of Rs.1,985 crore, were sold within days of the launch.

21%: The share of Indian stock brokers in commercial paper issuance in 2026, up from 4% in 2021. Brokers have raised about $33 billion, mainly to fund leveraged equity bets.

$102 million: The amount spent by Google co-founder Sergey Brin to oppose California's proposed billionaire wealth tax, making him the largest contributor to the campaign against it.

7: The number of countries, including India, that have expressed interest in hosting the 2036 Summer Olympics. The other six are Germany, Hungary, Qatar, South Africa, South Korea and Turkey.

India's second-largest telecom service provider Bharti Airtel has increased the prices of its postpaid plans by about 3-11%, its largest such price hike since 2024. The move comes days ahead of the expected initial public offering (IPO) of Jio Platforms, the parent of Reliance Jio, which is India's largest telecom operator by subscribers.

A raise in tariffs by Airtel could pave the way for Jio to follow suit, potentially giving it an opportunity to increase prices. Airtel last raised its headline tariffs in June 2024, after a gap of two years, following Jio. In the first quarter of 2026-27, Airtel recorded an average revenue per user (ARPU) of Rs.264. The company has been raising its ARPU, but the pace of annual growth has varied, with 2025-26 recording the lowest increase over a five-year period.

India finished the 2026 Asian Games with 85 medals, as a late gold rush helped it retain fourth place in the medals table behind China, Japan and South Korea. Its tally, however, was 21 medals lower than the 106 it won at the 2022 Hangzhou Asiad. India won medals in 20 of the 43 sports at this year's Games, but 76 of its 85 medals came from just 11 sports.

Athletics and shooting remained its two biggest medal-winning sports, although India won fewer medals in both than it did in 2022. The performance was unchanged from 2022 in seven of the other 11 sports that contributed to this year's tally, while India won more medals in the remaining two-boxing and golf.

data.title: Is HAL stock priced for perfection? What to expect over the next 5 years
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Indian defence stocks have faced periods of selling pressure over the past year after a strong multi-year rally.

Concerns around elevated valuations, profit booking, execution delays, and supply-chain challenges have led to sharp corrections across several defence names, including Hindustan Aeronautics (HAL).

HAL has posted negative returns of 1.47% over the past year, according to NSE data, compared to a positive 1.62% return for the Nifty Next 50 index.

Today, we examine the factors that could determine where HAL's stock could be in the next five years. But first, let's find out what the company is all about.

HAL is a major Indian aerospace and defence company that manufactures and maintains fighter aircraft, helicopters, aircraft engines, and other aerospace systems.

It is also involved in the development and production of platforms such as the Tejas light combat aircraft and Dhruv helicopters, as well as providing repair, overhaul, and maintenance services.

HAL entered FY27 with a robust order book of Rs.2.54 trillion. Management expects further growth in its deal pipeline, with key contracts-including 143 Advanced Light Helicopters (ALH) for the Indian Army, the IAF's Su-30 fleet upgrade, and the modernization of 40 Dornier Do-228 aircraft-currently at various stages of clearance.

In total, the company expects to bag fresh orders worth Rs.90,000 crore over the next two years, including repair and overhaul (ROH) contracts. However, its long-term performance hinges heavily on its ability to execute and deliver on these commitments on time.

To meet its large existing order book, handle anticipated new contracts, and ensure timely client deliveries, HAL has expanded manufacturing capacity for major programs. Production of the Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) and HTT-40 basic trainer has been scaled up across its Bengaluru and Nashik facilities, while Light Combat Helicopter (LCH) manufacturing at the Bengaluru and Tumakuru plants remains a core focus going forward.

Looking ahead, HAL plans to build dedicated manufacturing infrastructure for the LCA Mark-II, GE 414 engines, and Indian Multi-Role Helicopter (IMRH) engines. The expansion plan also includes infrastructure for Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) manufacturing, aero-engine indigenization projects, and design and development facilities for the IMRH and other defense programs.

The firm plans to invest about Rs.12,000 crore in these capital expenditure projects by 2030. Successfully converting this order book into timely deliveries and revenue recognition will be a decisive driver of the stock's performance over the next five years.

On top-line performance, HAL management remains confident of sustaining double-digit revenue growth through FY26 and FY27. On profitability, the company aims to protect its historically strong Ebitda margin baseline of 30-31%.

HAL remains a net debt-free company. Over the past five years, it has delivered consistent bottom-line performance, posting an average net profit growth of 22.9%. Also, its robust internal cash generation provides sufficient liquidity to fund upcoming capital expenditure plans.

HAL builds complex defense platforms such as the Tejas LCA and Light Combat Helicopters, requiring thousands of intricate components spanning avionics, engines, and weapon systems. In advanced aerospace manufacturing where tolerance for error is minimal, a single glitch during design, testing, or assembly can trigger multi-month operational delays. Having previously faced setbacks such as delayed General Electric (GE) engine deliveries, execution bottlenecks remain one of the primary risks facing the company.

Foreign-sourced critical parts expose HAL to delays, import restrictions, and cost volatility, amplifying execution bottlenecks despite. Manpower shortages for skilled engineers and MSME supply chain gaps further hinder scaling production to meet strict ministry of defence timelines.

According to a recent ICRA report, sales to the Indian defence forces account for more than 90% of the company's operating revenue. Although the company is trying to diversify its revenue base by increasing the share of orders from other clients and exports, a single customer still contributes heavily.

HAL trades at a price-to-earnings (P/E) multiple of 34.5, which is above its five-year median P/E of 30.7. Also, at a price-to-book (P/B) multiple of 7.3, the stock's valuation appears rich.

HAL's long-term growth prospects remain bright, anchored by a massive order backlog, expanding national defense budgets, solid balance sheet fundamentals, and the government's push for local manufacturing.

However, the stock's performance over the next five years will hinge entirely on execution, specifically HAL's capacity to convert its order pipeline into timely deliveries and recognized revenue. Seamless production scaling across the Tejas fighter and helicopter programs, engine availability, and supply chain management will be paramount.

At 34.5 times earnings, the stock offers limited valuation cushion, meaning any project execution delays could weigh on shareholder returns.

Investors should always evaluate a company's fundamentals, corporate governance, and stock valuations before making an investment decision.

Happy investing!

data.title: Best of the Week | An 'epiphany', a complaint and 36 caveats: Inside the Tata Trusts rift
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Best of the Week is a weekly newsletter by Siddharth Sharma/Shravani Sinha. Subscribe to Mint's newsletters to get them directly in your inbox.

The Tata boardroom drama has now moved into the trustees' room, and the letters are getting sharper.

Noel Tata and three fellow trustees of the Sir Dorabji Tata Trust (SDTT) have sent a five-page letter to colleagues Venu Srinivasan and Vijay Singh. Its target is their public backing for listing Tata Sons, which the letter sarcastically calls an "epiphany" that struck in April. The four say the pair never raised the idea at three SDTT board meetings since April and chose the media over their co-trustees instead. The letter also lays bare the arithmetic inside SDTT: four trustees on one side, two on the other.

SDTT owns 27.98% of Tata Sons, the holding company of India's largest conglomerate, and the letter says the Trusts' settled position has long been to keep it unlisted. Then came 17 September, when the Tata Sons board outvoted Noel to give N Chandrasekaran a third term as chairman and began moving towards a listing. Srinivasan voted with the majority.

There is a procedural sub-plot too. After the board backed a listing, Tata Trusts suggested on 28 September that Tata Sons could merge two subsidiaries to drop their core investment company and non-banking financial company tags. Singh and Srinivasan said they were not consulted. The four trustees counter that the Tata Sons board itself asked the Trusts to work on options for complying with the RBI's communication, and that Srinivasan was in the room.

Now the regulator has entered the picture. On 25 September, Srinivasan and Singh filed complaints with the Maharashtra Charity Commissioner, alleging SDTT's direct involvement in Tata Sons' commercial affairs and interference with the independent decision-making of nominee directors. Srinivasan has also urged action against any wrongdoing an investigation finds, including the possible suspension or removal of Noel as SDTT chairman. The commissioner has given SDTT until 12 October to reply.

Noel's camp sees an irony. The two who are asking for collective deliberation, they say, had already asked the regulator to stop the trustees from meeting at all, and never told the Trusts about their complaints. The four trustees now hope both complaints will be withdrawn. Will they be?

Precedent adds spice. In May, the commissioner barred the Sir Ratan Tata Trust, which owns 23.56% of Tata Sons, from holding meetings or taking decisions, after Srinivasan alleged that its permanent trustees exceeded a state limit.

Noel and his son Neville are not waiting around. On 1 October, they filed 21 and 15 caveats respectively with the commissioner, hoping to be heard before any order lands. The timing is interesting, because the Trusts' combined 65.9% voting power in Tata Sons could count for a great deal.

Meanwhile, the letter insists the Trusts neither run Tata Sons nor seek to. Their shareholding is the principal asset funding their charitable work, it says, and protecting it is stewardship, not business. Srinivasan and Singh see things very differently, and that disagreement may now be for the regulator to weigh.

The RBI's first rate hike in nearly four years was only the opening act. Now the aftershocks are arriving. Borrowers are bracing for higher EMIs or longer tenures, and consumer stocks have already slipped as investors fear a hit to festive spending. Banks, flush with liquidity, may find the hike a welcome cushion for their margins. Behind it all is inflation. Economists polled by Mint expect September's retail inflation to hit a 23-month high, with pressure spreading beyond a few food items. The central bank has also signalled that more hikes may follow.

Washington's visa crackdown is hitting trouble in court, yet opening a new front elsewhere. Two US courts have pushed Trump's $100,000 H-1B fee towards a dead end, finding the administration overreached. But the White House has not blinked. The US has now suspended green card labour certifications for six big outsourcing firms, including TCS, Infosys and Wipro, citing ongoing investigations. For India's IT majors, the immediate damage may be limited. They account for under 2% of such applications, and existing employees can keep working. The bigger worry is: what happens to the talent these firms most want to keep?

Mumbai airport's makeover has turned into a tug of war, and passengers are caught in the middle. Adani-run MIAL wanted to cut about a third of weekly international departure slots from 25 October to make room during Terminal 1's rebuild, with some flights heading to Navi Mumbai, 50 km away. Airlines said no, pointing to schedules approved months ago and asking why the cuts were needed. Now the civil aviation ministry has hit pause and sent everyone back to find common ground after 13 October. Adani insists the move is temporary. But for flyers, a different airport could mean higher fees and messier connections.

Angel One once won customers with printed research and branch networks. Then the internet rewrote the rules, and it went fully digital. Now the 30-year-old broker is reinventing itself again. It has shed nearly a fifth of its workforce as rivals Groww and Zerodha pull ahead on profits. Tighter derivatives rules and a shrinking pool of active investors are squeezing the business that once fuelled its growth. Its answer is a "super app" that bundles broking, mutual funds, insurance and credit under one roof. The bet is that existing customers will do more with the company.

India has become cheaper, yet foreign investors keep heading for the exit. That is the mystery haunting Dalal Street. Through September, net foreign equity outflows hit Rs.2.60 trillion, and the Nifty trailed every global peer Mint tracked. Meanwhile, Asian rivals riding the AI and semiconductor wave raced ahead.

But look at the primary market and the story shifts. Foreign investors have been net buyers there every single month this year. So have they really given up on India, or are they simply getting choosier? And what would it take to bring them back? Experts point to earnings upgrades, a steadier rupee and softer crude.

After building a Rs.48,178 crore-income lending business, Shriram Group is making a bigger push into capital markets, betting on India's growing appetite for investments. Its revamped business will combine broking, mutual funds and wealth management, using digital tools alongside human advice to reach investors beyond big cities.

The group is rebuilding Way2Wealth as an advice-led platform, with plans to expand margin trading finance. But the timing is tricky: volatile, range-bound markets threaten brokerage revenues, while established players dominate the space. Can Shriram turn its vast lending customer base into a new generation of investors?

Sebi's investor protection fund has nearly quadrupled to Rs.969.8 crore in FY26, but spending has barely budged. The regulator used just Rs.4.7 crore, or 0.4% of the corpus, even as financial-influencer scams, online investment frauds and digital arrests proliferate. A Sebi survey found 62% of investors base some or most investment decisions on finfluencer recommendations. The underutilization has caught the government's attention, though no decision has been made on intervention. Experts argue the fund could do more, from financing cybersecurity research to expanding investor awareness, while calling for greater transparency on spending and outcomes.

India's staffing firms are moving beyond supplying workers to being accountable for their performance. Quess Corp, TeamLease Services and Adecco are seeing growing demand for output-based billing, where vendors face penalties or lose fees if workers miss client targets.

About 10-15% of Quess clients already seek some form of output-driven service. The model can command fees of 10-20% per candidate, compared with 9-10% under traditional staffing. Rising labour costs and absenteeism are driving adoption, while AI-led productivity gains are pushing clients to pay for outcomes rather than activity. Adoption remains at an early stage.

Mercedes-Benz and BMW are bringing global models to India faster, shrinking launch delays from 10-12 months to around 4-6 months as buyers demand access to the latest vehicles. Mercedes plans to introduce its GLC electric model six months after its European debut, while BMW has brought some performance models within three to four months.

Right-hand-drive conversions and regulatory certification remain hurdles. The push reflects India's growing importance and rising demand for premium vehicles. Mercedes sold a record 15,190 cars in January-September 2026, up 8% year-on-year, while BMW's April-June deliveries rose 17% to 4,507.

Women's commutes in India reveal a stark gender divide, according to the first National Household Travel Survey, covering 1.8 million people. The share of rural women travelling over 1 km to work is just 37.7%, against 64.2% travelling for education. In cities, the share falls from 67.5% to 52.9%. Rural women largely walk to work, while urban women rely more on buses and other public transport. Men depend heavily on two-wheelers. Safety also shapes travel patterns, with women generally leaving work earlier. Men typically spend more on commuting each month.

That's all from us this week. Subscribe to our newsletters and the website for what's in the news and beyond it. Write to us at newsletters@livemint.com.

data.title: SpaceX's Spectrum Deal Could Boost AST SpaceMobile’s Strategic Value — Analyst Calls ASTS 'Natural Satellite Partner' For Carriers
data.description:
Key points:
  • Berenberg maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on AST SpaceMobile following Grain Management’s agreement to sell its nationwide spectrum portfolio to SpaceX.
  • According to Filatov, SpaceX's decision to build out its own network could make AST SpaceMobile “more strategically relevant” rather than simply increasing competitive pressure.
  • He cited SpaceX positioning itself as a mobile carrier rather than simply a satellite connectivity provider as the reason for his optimism around AST SpaceMobile.

Space Exploration Technologies Corp.’s (SPCX) latest push into mobile connectivity could be creating an unexpected opportunity for AST SpaceMobile Inc. (ASTS), analysts at Berenberg said.

The satellite-to-phone race is increasingly becoming a battle over not just technology, but who ultimately controls the customer relationship. According to TheFly, Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov believes SpaceX’s latest move could sharpen the strategic distinction between the two companies.

AST SpaceMobile shares fell more than 10% on Friday, declining 0.1% further during the after-hours trade. SpaceX shares gained more than 1% during the regular trading session, and rose 0.1% further in the after-hours trade.

SpaceX’s Mobile Ambitions Could Boost ASTS

Berenberg maintained a ‘Buy’ rating on AST SpaceMobile following Grain Management’s agreement to sell its nationwide spectrum portfolio to SpaceX, subject to Federal Communications Commission approval.

The deal involves up to 14 MHz of paired spectrum in the 800 MHz band, giving SpaceX access to low-band spectrum that it says will help close a key technical gap for its Starlink Mobile ambitions.

SpaceX described the move as a step toward building the world’s “most advanced” mobile network. The company said the low-band spectrum will complement its existing 2 GHz mid-band spectrum, with the new frequencies providing a coverage layer capable of improving connectivity through obstacles such as walls.

Critically, SpaceX said most existing mobile devices already support the band, potentially allowing Starlink Mobile to provide connectivity without requiring users to replace their phones.

SpaceX said its goal is to combine its satellite constellation with a terrestrial network into a single architecture that can provide connectivity “indoors, outdoors, in cellular dead zones, and everywhere in between.”

Berenberg sees that strategy as an important development for AST SpaceMobile.

ASTS Could Become The ‘Natural Satellite Partner’

According to Filatov, SpaceX's decision to build out its own network could make AST SpaceMobile “more strategically relevant” rather than simply increasing competitive pressure. He cited SpaceX positioning itself as a mobile carrier rather than simply a satellite connectivity provider as the reason for his optimism around AST SpaceMobile.

That could leave ASTS with a potentially valuable position in the market, which is partnering with existing telecom operators rather than competing against them, the analyst said.

Filatov argues that AST SpaceMobile is currently the only device-to-device operator whose technology is designed to deliver broadband connectivity to existing smartphones while maintaining a carrier-partnership model.

The analyst therefore sees AST SpaceMobile as “the natural satellite partner for operators.”

SPCX Gets Another Boost From FCC

The spectrum deal wasn't SpaceX’s only major mobile-network milestone this week.

The FCC also approved SpaceX’s Gen2 Starlink constellation application, authorizing the company to launch 15,000 satellites optimized for 2 GHz spectrum globally.

SpaceX said its V2 Starlink Mobile satellites will deliver more than 100 times the bandwidth of its current generation and provide high-speed connectivity directly to unmodified devices.

The FCC also authorized the full range of backhaul bands used by SpaceX’s V3 broadband satellites, allowing them to operate with Starlink’s existing gateway network.

SpaceX said the approvals will help advance its vision of keeping users connected “no matter where they are,” from dense cities to remote and rural areas.

data.title: RBI steps up rupee support, opens dollar window for oil companies
data.description:
Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has announced more ​measures to support the rupee on Saturday after the ‌currency fell to within striking distance of ​its record low.

RBI will open a special window to meet the daily dollar requirements of three government oil-marketing companies to ‌ease the pressure on the spot market.

Under such an arrangement, used in ‌times of strain on the currency, the RBI ‌provides ⁠oil companies dollars directly from its foreign ⁠exchange reserves.

Indian Oil, Hindustan Petroleum and Bharat Petroleum will be allowed to access dollars under the facility from ​Monday, the RBI said.

Forex dealers will not permit users to rebook any foreign exchange derivatives, the bank said.

The RBI slashed the limit for positions in ‌exchange-traded currency derivatives involving the rupee to $5 million ​from $100 million.

The central bank asked forex dealers to maintain a “foreign exchange risk reserve” ⁠for all derivative contracts involving the rupee equal to 20 per cent of the notional amount of each transaction.

The RBI has raised dollars and hiked its policy rate, but pressure on the currency has persisted. On Friday, the rupee closed at 96.73 per dollar, barely changed from its previous close, and near its all-time weakest level of 96.96, hit in ‌May.

The rupee rallied in the non-deliverable forward market ​on Saturday, with the one-month dollar/rupee contract falling about 40 paise in very thin trading, ⁠one trader said.

Addressing oil companies’ dollar requirements ⁠removes one of the largest sources of demand from the FX market, which should help reduce ‌volatility but it will show up in a depletion of reserves, said Dhiraj Nim, FX ​strategist at ANZ Bank in Mumbai.

data.title: Wall Street posts weekly gains with earnings, inflation data on tap
data.description:

data.title: BlackRock ETF clients buy $22.38 million worth of Bitcoin
data.description:
BlackRock's Bitcoin ETF clients added $22.38 million worth of Bitcoin, extending the fund's pattern of steady, if uneven, demand.

Farside Investors data shows the iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) recorded a net inflow of $22.4 million on October 9, 2026.

A net inflow is simple arithmetic. It is the money investors put into the fund minus the money they pulled out.

BlackRock does not keep that Bitcoin in its own vault. Custody of IBIT's holdings sits with Coinbase Prime, the institutional arm of the US exchange.

The October 9 inflow came during a choppy stretch for the fund. On October 7, IBIT saw a $207.7 million outflow, a far larger move in the opposite direction.

Earlier in October, the fund pulled in $195.6 million within the first week of the month.

Bitcoin's price has recently hovered in a range between $78,700 and $85,000.

IBIT is BlackRock's flagship US spot Bitcoin ETF. A spot ETF holds the actual asset rather than futures contracts, so every share is backed by real Bitcoin.

The fund is the largest US spot Bitcoin ETF by assets under management, and leads the category in cumulative flows. Total inflows since launch have exceeded $65 billion.

Broader US spot Bitcoin ETF flows were mixed in early October 2026. IBIT often led inflows on positive days, while the category as a whole saw periods of net outflows.

In July 2026, BlackRock cut the minimum threshold for in-kind Bitcoin-to-IBIT conversions from $25 million to $1 million. An in-kind conversion lets an investor hand over Bitcoin directly in exchange for ETF shares, instead of selling coins for cash first. The program has processed over $5 billion in such swaps.

data.title: Life insurers projected to post 10-20% VNB growth in 2QFY27: Report
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 10 -- Life insurance companies in India are likely to register a 10 to 20 per cent year-on-year growth in value of new business (VNB) during the second quarter of FY27, even as broader discussions focus heavily on proposed regulatory guidelines rather than quarterly operational prints, according to a research report by Kotak Institutional Equities.

The brokerage noted that private life insurers under its coverage show steady underwriting performance, driven largely by solid expansion in protection plans despite moderate annualised premium equivalent (APE) growth.

"We expect 2QFY27 earnings call discussion and stock price performance to be centered around the impact of the proposed distribution norms and EoM guidelines, with less emphasis on the quarterly financial performance itself," the report stated.

"Growth in protection is supporting margins and VNB despite moderate (10-15% yoy for the private sector) APE growth. Health claims tend to inch up in 2Q, though secular improvements and higher leverage continue to drive core earnings; trends in motor TP claims provisioning will drive the performance of non-life companies for the quarter. PB will continue on a steady growth path," the report added.

Analyzing company-level performances across the life insurance basket, the brokerage projects private insurers to record 10 to 15 per cent APE growth with a 6 to 18 per cent increase in VNB, alongside net margin shifts ranging between negative 200 basis points and positive 150 basis points. State-owned Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) is projected to outpace private peers on profitability, delivering an estimated 320 basis points of margin expansion to 22.5 per cent on the back of higher non-participating product share, which drives a 40 per cent surge in its VNB.

"We expect private life insurers under coverage to deliver 10-15% APE growth with 6-18% growth in VNB. We bake in -200 to +150 bps expansion in margins. The positive drivers are high growth in the protection business, ending the controversy on margin loss due to GST exemption. We do not expect a notable product mix change in the savings business," the report said.

Regarding the wider regulatory and medium-term operational environment, the research agency highlighted that proposed caps on expenses of management (EoM) and distribution commissions represent the primary variables shaping forward outlooks.

"With sweeping changes proposed in distribution payouts and EoM cap, we expect management discussions to be dominated by the same-loss of VNB due to likely lower credit protect business, channel strategy, open or closed architecture in banks, dependence on PB and ability to meet EoM norms," the report said.

It mentioned that the near-term growth outlook is likely to be strong due to the sunset period and the weakness in FY2028E (to initially adjust to new norms and then a high base) do not reflect the new normal.

"In the meanwhile, the IRDA will draft new norms on products, customer redressal and claims; we expect IFRS 17 and RBC to also be implemented. Hence, stocks will remain under pressure of uncertainty even as valuation remains un-demanding," the report stated.

In the non-life insurance space, claims ratios in motor third-party (TP) policies will set operating trends for the quarter following judicial pronouncements regarding homemaker compensation.
